headline: Firefox 156 arrives amid a sea of alternatives
standfirst: The browser landscape is expanding as users increasingly turn to custom forks of Firefox.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Firefox 156 is here, but it is sharing the stage with a growing number of alternative versions.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Over time, many users became dissatisfied with Mozilla. They created their own spin-off browsers.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Browsers like Waterfox, LibreWolf, and Pale Moon show that people want more control and choice.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: See if these niche browsers can keep up with the rapid update pace of the main Firefox release.

caption:
Firefox 156 has launched, but many users are choosing to stick with browser forks like LibreWolf and Waterfox.

The open-source nature of Firefox allows developers to create custom versions tailored to specific needs. These forks often appeal to users looking for different privacy settings or interface tweaks that the official browser does not offer. It highlights a fragmented but active community of Mozilla dissenters.
